title: Mechanics Foundations — Internal Assessment Blueprint

assessmentPurposes.diagnostic: Identify prior misconceptions, missing prerequisites, sign-convention weaknesses, graph-reading weaknesses, and force-motion misconceptions.
assessmentPurposes.formative: Evaluate concept comprehension, representation switching, formula selection, reasoning quality, calculation processes, and misconception corrections.
assessmentPurposes.exit: Determine if the student can describe motion, select representation, apply constant-acceleration equations, interpret graphs, and reason with Newton's First Law and Inertia.

slots.learningObjective: Explain the relativity of rest and motion by comparing passenger observations from train and platform frames.
slots.expectedReasoning: Explains that motion is frame-dependent; sitting passenger is at rest relative to the train carriage but moving relative to the ground platform.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Clearly identifies that state of motion differs across coordinate systems and rejects absolute rest.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Selecting absolute answers ('is strictly at rest').
slots.commonFailureSignals: Assuming the platform ground is the only reference frame.
slots.masterySignal: Correct option selection and choice of frame-dependent explanation.

slots.learningObjective: Distinguish between total path distance and straight-line displacement in a 1D turn-back scenario.
slots.expectedReasoning: Recognizes that distance accumulates positively over the entire path, while displacement depends only on final and initial positions.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Correct distance calculation and displacement calculation with sign.
slots.commonFailureSignals: Adding individual segment lengths to get displacement.
slots.masterySignal: Correctly computes both values with units.

slots.learningObjective: Calculate average speed and average velocity vector for a two-segment 1D motion where the object reverses direction.
slots.expectedReasoning: Divides total distance by total time for average speed, and net displacement by total time for average velocity.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Obtains different values for speed and velocity due to the directional reversal, with correct signs/vectors.
slots.masterySignal: Correct numerical outputs with correct units.

slots.learningObjective: Explain that a negative velocity indicates direction of motion in 1D rather than magnitude changes.
slots.expectedReasoning: Identifies that an object moving in the negative direction is speeding up if its acceleration is also negative.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Explains that sign designates direction and speed is the absolute magnitude.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Stating that a negative sign automatically implies deceleration.
slots.commonFailureSignals: Confusing signed values with physical speeds.
slots.criticalError: Conflating negative sign with speed reduction.
slots.masterySignal: Correctly identifies speed changes under different sign combinations.

slots.learningObjective: Determine whether an object is stationary, moving forward, or reversing by analyzing the position-time (x-t) graph slope.
slots.expectedReasoning: Interrogates the slope of the curve at specific points, matching zero slope to rest and high height to position only.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Distinguishes high-position/low-speed states from low-position/high-speed states on the graph.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Treating the vertical position coordinate as velocity.
slots.commonFailureSignals: Reading the y-axis value as speed.
slots.masterySignal: Accurately computes slope at multiple intervals and identifies motion state.

slots.learningObjective: Calculate acceleration and displacement from the slope and signed area of a velocity-time (v-t) graph.
slots.expectedReasoning: Employs slope for acceleration and area for displacement, tracking positive and negative areas.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Calculates net displacement using signed areas and acceleration using slope, correctly resolving units.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Adding areas absolute values for displacement or using position formula without graph data.
slots.masterySignal: Correctly evaluates both acceleration and signed displacement from the graph.

slots.learningObjective: Define constant acceleration and explain how velocity can be zero momentarily while acceleration is non-zero.
slots.expectedReasoning: Explains that acceleration is the rate of change of velocity; velocity can pass through zero when changing direction (like a ball at peak height).
slots.acceptableEvidence: Demonstrates that v=0 doesn't require a=0 if velocity is changing.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Stating that because velocity is zero, there is no change in motion.
slots.commonFailureSignals: Equating instantaneous velocity value to rate of change.
slots.criticalError: Stating acceleration is zero at peak.
slots.masterySignal: Provides correct conceptual description of peak vertical flight state.

slots.learningObjective: Select the correct kinematic equation for constant acceleration based on given/find parameters.
slots.expectedReasoning: Matches variables to isolate the formula missing the unknown/unnecessary parameter.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Selects appropriate equations for various parameter sets without executing arithmetic.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Randomly guessing formulas or selecting equations containing multiple unknown parameters.
slots.masterySignal: 100% correct matching across three separate scenarios.

slots.learningObjective: Execute a multi-step calculation using UAM equations and perform a dimensional/sanity check.
slots.expectedReasoning: Calculates displacement and final velocity for freefall, verifying that mass does not enter kinematic relations.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Correct numerical substitution, units, and explanation of mass-independence.
slots.commonFailureSignals: Attempting to include mass in the kinematic formulas.
slots.criticalError: Entering mass into the kinematic equations.
slots.masterySignal: Correct numerical output, correct units, and correct mass-independence reasoning.

slots.learningObjective: Explain Newton's First Law and identify that constant velocity implies zero net force.
slots.expectedReasoning: Deduces that if velocity is constant, acceleration is zero, which requires balanced external forces.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Rejects the need for a active forward force to maintain constant speed in frictionless environments.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Believing a net force must exist in the direction of motion for an object to continue moving.
slots.commonFailureSignals: Conflating velocity direction with net force direction.
slots.criticalError: Claiming a forward force is needed.
slots.masterySignal: Correct option selection for a constant velocity spacecraft/frictionless case.

slots.learningObjective: Relate an object's mass to its translational inertia and compare the resistance to changes in motion.
slots.expectedReasoning: Mass is the quantitative measure of inertia. A heavier object has more resistance to acceleration, not an active force pushing back.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Explains inertia as an inherent property of mass and not a force vector.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Stating that inertia is a force acting against motion.
slots.commonFailureSignals: Classifying inertia as a reactive force.
slots.criticalError: Modeling inertia as a reactive force vector.
slots.masterySignal: Correct choice identifying mass as the measure of inertia and rejecting inertia as a force.

slots.learningObjective: Analyze an integrated scenario containing a constant velocity segment and a constant acceleration segment, verifying correct force-motion mapping.
slots.requiredRepresentation: qualitative force diagram reasoning, velocity-time graph
slots.expectedReasoning: Links zero acceleration in v-t graph to zero net force, and non-zero constant slope to constant net force.
slots.acceptableEvidence: Demonstrates correct mapping of force states to kinematic motion states.
slots.insufficientEvidence: Assuming force is proportional to velocity at all points.
slots.commonFailureSignals: Recommending force during uniform motion segment.
slots.masterySignal: Provides clear, logical reasoning linking graph properties to force states.

masteryStateProvisional.REVIEW_REQUIRED: Adequate points but unresolved critical misconception or atom coverage gap.
masteryStateProvisional.FOUNDATIONAL_GAP: Obtained less than 50% points, or fails in basic prerequisite or representation check.
masteryStateProvisional.NOT_ASSESSED: Blueprint slots not yet mapped to items.

masteryRules.note: Provisional masteries are internal assessment parameters only and do not represent publish readiness or student declarations.
